residue.text: Retained stage1 limitation: motor-off does not guarantee stopped circulation. Shared-volume history survives; transfer timing and gradient state differ. Inspect frames and report residual motion. Similar results question commanded concurrency necessity; different results cannot isolate coupling from timing or transfer disturbance.

Source-bound proposals omitted from the six-trial interface block remain unexecuted: fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds without optical restart; enabled versus timer-stopped 900 rpm; matched fixed-speed and brief stir-off comparisons. These test necessity, feedback and the reversed agitation-to-image arrow. Hypothesized successes remain unknown; cessation times and unequal quiet durations limit attribution.

Retained anomaly: 900 rpm spreads fluctuate 11, 3, 12 percent with approximately 12 mm depression and transient specks. Matched final vials and isolated bubble measurements are absent. Specks do not identify bubbles. Disturbance-renewing feedback remains a hypothesis; persistent artifacts or genuine gradients remain rivals.

Retained concerns: reference repeatability is not concentration calibration; sampling and transfers can disturb gradients; commanded rpm lacks independent verification. One lower-speed success establishes neither reliable sufficiency nor combined-operation advantage. Relative stirring-time savings lack the preferred duration. Other conditions and real chemical or human benefits remain unsupported.

summary.text: Hypothesis under test: concurrent rotation and low-to-high syringe redistribution are necessary for this fixed pair of parent doses. Stage1 defines the interface as commanded temporal overlap. The supplied concerns retain the observed 300 rpm final-vial spread of approximately 2.4 percent without redistribution, a bounded counterexample to universal 900 rpm necessity, not proof of coupling or feedback.

Proposed arms retain nominal 300 rpm at seconds 0-15, 30-45, 60-75 and 90-105, totaling 60 stirring seconds. Both perform three marked 10 mL low withdrawals and upper-side returns within five seconds each. Coupled transfers occupy 10-15, 40-45, 70-75; staggered transfers occupy 25-30, 55-60, 85-90 after ten commanded-off seconds. Optical checks never control operation.

Propose three fresh pairs within six trials: prescribed 150 mL water and 0.30 mL dye, rinsed vessel, fixed addition location, one bottle, locked camera, reversed arm order, spill tray and escape stop. Finish by 105; sample depths 10, 28, 45 mm from 120 within ten seconds, alternating order. Report raw attenuation, spread, duration, transfers, depression, specks and failures. Target is at most 4 percent sample spread; stable images alone cannot establish it.

Hypothesis predictions: effective overlap ablation would yield coupled success and reproducible staggered failure if concurrency matters; reproducible staggered success would question its necessity. Both failing leaves accounts unresolved. These future outcomes are unobserved; independent depth samples retain the supplied concerns about optical evidence and measurement disturbance.
